chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, said: I took a copy of the letter of al-Mutawakkil to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام from Yahya ibn Harthamah in the year two hundred and forty-three, and this is its copy.

In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. To proceed: the Commander of the Faithful recognizes your worth, observes your kinship, and deems your right obligatory. He considers, regarding you and the people of your household, such matters by which Allah may rectify your condition and theirs, confirm your honor and their honor, and bring blessing and security upon you and upon them, seeking thereby the pleasure of his Lord and the fulfillment of what has been made obligatory upon him concerning you and concerning them.

And the Commander of the Faithful has seen fit to remove Abdullah ibn Muhammad from what he had been overseeing of war and salat (prayer) in the city of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, since he was as you mentioned regarding his ignorance of your right and his belittling of your worth, and because of what he imputed to you and ascribed to you of the matter from which the Commander of the Faithful knows your innocence, and the truthfulness of your intention in refraining from pursuing it, and that you did not put yourself forward for it.

And the Commander of the Faithful has appointed over that Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, and ordered him to honor you, revere you, comply with your command and your view, and seek nearness to Allah and to the Commander of the Faithful through that. And the Commander of the Faithful longs for you and loves to renew acquaintance with you and to look upon you. So if you are inclined to visit him and remain in his presence for whatever duration you see fit, then you may set out, together with whomever you wish from your household, your mawali, and your attendants, in ease and tranquility, departing when you wish, halting when you wish, and traveling however you wish.

And if you would like Yahya ibn Harthamah, the mawla of the Commander of the Faithful, and those with him from the troops, to accompany you, departing with your departure and traveling with your travel, then the decision in that is left to you until you arrive before the Commander of the Faithful.

For there is no one among his brothers, his children, the people of his household, and his close associates who holds a more gracious position with him, nor for whom his preference is more praiseworthy; nor is he more considerate toward them, more compassionate toward them, more dutiful with them, or more reassuring to them, than he is toward you, if Allah the Exalted wills. And peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings. Written by Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his family and grant peace.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the ruling caliph, referred to here in official court language
key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِكَ: the Imam’s household and family members
key_terms.بَرَاءَتَكَ: your innocence and disavowal from the accusation
key_terms.تَبْجِيلِكَ: showing you reverence and exalted respect
key_terms.جَهَالَتِهِ: his ignorance, referring to Abdullah ibn Muhammad’s lack of recognition of the Imam’s right
key_terms.مَوَالِيكَ: your close associates or dependents attached to your household
key_terms.مُشَيِّعِينَ: those accompanying and escorting you on the journey

ai.seo_question: What does al-Mutawakkil’s letter to Imam al-Hadi عليه السلام say about his summons from al-Madinah?
ai.summary: This report preserves the text of al-Mutawakkil’s letter to Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام, inviting him from al-Madinah and presenting the move as an act of honor and concern. It is historically significant for documenting the political circumstances surrounding the Imam’s summons and the official language used toward Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
